text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency spike detected in runtime-prod after rollout (deploy_id=deploy-760555). Error rate rising ~4% -> 12% over last 3m. Affected routes: /v1/generate (mostly long-seq). Auto-escalation: paging oncall.

sre-jen: I'm on it, grabbing logs. initial hypothesis: kernel-selector fell back to generic kernel -> batch sizes collapsed, queuing spike.

maya-product: Customers reporting slow responses and timeouts, some 503s. Taking an incident bridge. @oncall-tom can you join? :phone:

oncall-tom: joining bridge now. any quick mitigation we can flip?

eli-eng: The rollout enabled a new "wildcard-routing" flag that widened model variant routing. It looks like it pushed traffic to a variant without the quantized kernels for long sequences. Kernel fallback seen in nodes: rtx-pool-12/14.

eli-eng: quick snippet from node logs:
```
[2026-03-17T14:22:18Z] kernel_selector: no optimized kernel found for model=redwood-v1-longseq -> fallback=generic_attention
[2026-03-17T14:22:18Z] batcher: active_batch_size=1 queued=64
[2026-03-17T14:22:19Z] inference: token_latency_ms=3200 p95
```

incident-bot: Incident severity increased to P1 due to customer impact metric threshold. Notifying support.

support-amy: We've flagged top 5 paying customers; CS is proactively emailing. No major L2 escalations yet but slow UX reports.

eli-eng: Mitigation plan: 1) Flip feature flag wildcard-routing OFF (FF: fw/wildcard-routing). 2) If that doesn't recover within 2m, roll back deploy-760555. 3) Temporarily scale batcher workers + reduce max-concurrency to halve queuing pressure.

oncall-tom: I'm toggling the flag now: `/ff toggle fw/wildcard-routing off --env prod --actor tom`

sre-jen: Flag toggle acknowledged by infra: fw/wildcard-routing = OFF. Observability: p95 trending down from 3200ms -> 900ms in 45s. error rate stabilizing at ~5%.

eli-eng: Good sign. Still seeing some kernel fallback thrash on a subset of rtx nodes, draining those pods now: `kubectl drain node=rtx-pool-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then roll them to pickup optimized kernels.

oncall-tom: Drains in progress. Will keep bridge open for 30m and handoff to SRE rotation.

maya-product: Notifying customers with ETA ~15m for stabilization. Posting interim status to status.redwood.com :writing_hand: .

incident-bot: Post-action checklist created: assignable -> @sre-jen (root cause triage), @eli-eng (rollback/selector fix), @maya-product (customer comms).

support-amy: CS update posted. Affected customers: 5 contacted, no escalations to legal/security.

sre-jen: After drains and flag flip, metrics look near-normal but we'll keep additional autoscaling for 20m. Leaving handoff note: oncall rotation for next shift take SRE-rotation-2.

oncall-tom: Handoff to SRE-rotation-2 in 30m. Action items: (1) revert wildcard-routing code path that bypasses kernel hints, (2) add preflight check to reject routing wideners for long-sequence models, (3) run controlled canary with traffic caps next deploy.

eli-eng: I'll open a PR with the kernel-hint guard and add a rollout gate to the deploy pipeline.

sre-jen: Filing postmortem ticket: PM-INC-760555. High level: premature routing expansion caused fallback to generic kernels => batch collapse => latency spike.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Will monitor for 60m then close if stable.

maya-product: Thanks all. Great quick triage. :clap:

oncall-tom: closing bridge in 10. Handoff note posted in #oncall-handoffs.

sre-jen: leaving final note: no customer data exposure. will coordinate changelist with security review before next rollout.
